exposure: advanced maternal age at delivery (≥35 years)
high early pregnancy body mass index (≥30 kg/m(2))
cohort: Pregnant women at term undergoing labor induction
finding: Advanced maternal age (≥35 years), high early pregnancy BMI (≥30 kg/m2), nulliparity, low preinduction Bishop's score (<5), gestational diabetes mellitus, and intrauterine growth restriction were identified as risk factors for emergency cesarean delivery in women undergoing labor induction at term.
mod_finding: This study found that advanced maternal age, high BMI, nulliparity, low Bishop's score, gestational diabetes, and intrauterine growth restriction increased the risk of emergency cesarean delivery in induced labors at term.
